notes.claudeCode: Use single quotes so the ${'{'}KNOWLEDGE_API_KEY{'}'} placeholder is stored, not the key itself. Check with `claude mcp list`, then `/mcp` inside a session.
notes.codex: Codex reads the key from the variable named in bearer_token_env_var — no interpolation syntax. Verify with `codex mcp list`.
notes.gemini: Streamable HTTP needs httpUrl; plain url means SSE. The CLI defaults to project scope, hence --scope user. Check with `/mcp` in a session.
notes.cursor: Cursor expands ${'{'}env:VAR{'}'} in headers. Restart Cursor after exporting the variable so it inherits it, then enable the server under Settings → MCP.
notes.vscode: VS Code asks for the key once and stores it encrypted. ${'{'}env:…{'}'} in headers is currently sent literally by VS Code, so this uses a prompted input instead.
notes.claudeDesktop: Claude Desktop's config file runs local servers only, so mcp-remote bridges to this endpoint (Node.js required). The key is written into the file — keep it private. Restart Claude after saving.
notes.windsurf: Newer builds read ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json; older Windsurf builds ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json. Refresh the MCP list in Cascade after saving.
notes.opencode: oauth: false stops opencode trying OAuth against a key-authenticated server. Place it in opencode.json at the project root, or globally.
notes.zed: Zed has no environment-variable expansion in headers, so the key is written into settings.json. Or add it from Settings → AI → MCP Servers.
notes.http: Any MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP works: POST JSON-RPC with the bearer header. This call answers who the key acts as — a quick way to test a key.

reviewIntervalDays.label: Review interval

trustRanking.label: Trust-aware ranking
trustRanking.hint: Multiply search scores by each page's verification state, so verified pages rank above outdated ones

rrfK.label: Fusion constant (RRF k)
rrfK.hint: How strongly a top rank in one search leg outweighs agreement between both legs. Lower favours the single best match, higher favours pages both legs found

minCosine.label: Minimum similarity
minCosine.hint: A semantic match below this cosine is not a result at all, so a question nothing answers comes back empty instead of padded. The right value depends on the embedding model: about 0.4 for bge-m3. 0 turns it off

minCosineShare.label: Similarity band
minCosineShare.hint: A semantic match counts only within this share of the best one, so pages found at middling ranks by both legs cannot outrank the best match of either. 0 turns it off

communityPriorWeight.label: Community boost
communityPriorWeight.hint: How much a page gains when its community's summary matches the question: a page in the closest matching group scores up to this much higher (0.5 means ×1.5). Needs communities built by the Atlas agent. 0 turns it off

communityPriorFloor.label: Community match threshold
communityPriorFloor.hint: How closely a community's summary must match the question before it boosts anything. Higher boosts only clear matches. The right value depends on the embedding model: about 0.5 for bge-m3
communityPriorFloor.inert: The community boost is off, so this threshold changes nothing until a boost is set.

layeredExpansion.label: Expand related pages by layer

trustWeights.label: Trust weights

trustWeights.inert: Trust-aware ranking is off, so these weights change nothing until it is turned on.

connect.title: Connect a bot
connect.description: The token is checked with Telegram and stored encrypted. It is never shown again.
connect.step1: In Telegram, message BotFather and send /newbot.
connect.step2: Copy the token it gives you and paste it below.
connect.step3: Message your bot privately: it replies with a link that connects your account.

time.description: The token is checked with your Time server and stored encrypted. It is never shown again.
time.step1: In Time, open Integrations → Bot accounts and create a bot (bot creation must be allowed in your space).
time.step2: Copy the token it shows once, and paste it below with your Time server address.
time.step3: Add the bot to a channel and mention it, or message it privately: it replies with a link that connects your account.

mattermost.description: The token is checked with your Mattermost server and stored encrypted. It is never shown again.
mattermost.step1: In Mattermost, open Integrations → Bot Accounts and add a bot (a system admin may first need to enable bot account creation in the System Console).
mattermost.step2: Copy the access token it shows once, and paste it below with your Mattermost server address.
mattermost.step3: Add the bot to a team and a channel and mention it, or message it privately: it replies with a link that connects your account.

slack.description: The token is checked with Slack. The token and the signing secret are stored encrypted and never shown again.
slack.step1: At api.slack.com/apps, create an app from scratch in your workspace. It stays internal to that workspace; nothing is published.
slack.step2: Under OAuth & Permissions, add the bot token scopes chat:write, channels:history, groups:history, im:history and reactions:read, then install the app.
slack.step3: Paste the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) and, from Basic Information, the Signing Secret below.
slack.step4: Once connected, paste the address shown on the bot’s card as the Request URL under Event Subscriptions (bot events message.channels, message.groups, message.im, reaction_added) and under Interactivity. Then invite the bot to a channel and mention it, or message it privately to link your account.

teams.description: Microsoft checks the credential before anything is saved. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
teams.step1: In the Azure portal, create an Azure Bot of type Single Tenant. Copy its Microsoft App ID and its directory (tenant) ID, and create a client secret for its app registration.
teams.step2: Paste the three below. Once the bot is connected, set the address shown on its card as the bot’s Messaging endpoint (Configuration), and turn on the Microsoft Teams channel.
teams.step3: Install it in Teams with an app package whose manifest names the bot, and grants the resource-specific permission ChannelMessage.Read.Group so a channel can keep its messages for capture (manifest in the docs).
teams.step4: Mention the bot in a channel, or message it in a chat: it replies with a link that connects your account.

run.intro: Setup runs once, then every case (negative ones first), then teardown, which runs even after a failure. The values below are kept for this run only and sent only in the requests that use them.

auth.title: Credentials

apiTry.corsNoProxy: An admin can turn on the proxy in API reference settings, or send it from a terminal with the cURL sample.
apiTry.truncated: Cut at {size}; the response was longer.
apiTry.browserHeaders: A browser shows only the headers the API exposes to it (Access-Control-Expose-Headers).

runner.title: Server runs
runner.subtitle: Let the worker run a whole QA suite against a test environment, from the QA page or an agent. Each request goes out exactly as the try-it proxy sends it: the proxy mode above, its source policies, and only servers the spec declares.
runner.ceilingOff: This deployment keeps server runs off (API_TEST_RUNNER_MODE). Asking for them here takes effect once it allows them.

off.label: Off
off.body: Suites run from the browser or the proxy only. Nothing is sent from the server.

on.label: On
on.body: Members with “Run API tests” can run a suite on the server. Each run’s results are kept, the last 20 per suite.

apiSettings.title: API reference
apiSettings.subtitle: How the try-it console on spec pages may reach the APIs they describe.

proxy.title: Try-it proxy
proxy.subtitle: Requests go from the reader’s browser by default. The proxy sends them from the server instead, for APIs that refuse browser requests — only to servers the spec names, only for its operations, and only for editors.

off.label: Off
off.body: Every request goes from the reader’s browser. APIs without CORS cannot be tried.

allowlist.label: Allowlisted hosts
allowlist.body: The proxy reaches only hosts the workspace’s source policies allow.

open.label: Any public host
open.body: The proxy reaches any public host the source policies do not block. Private addresses stay refused.

apiSettings.clampExplained: This workspace asks for “{requested}”, but the deployment allows at most “{ceiling}” (API_TRY_PROXY_MODE), so “{ceiling}” is what applies.
apiSettings.limits: Per person: {perMinute} requests a minute, {timeout} s each, bodies up to {request} out and {response} back.
apiSettings.adminOnly: Only a workspace admin can change this.

breaking.title: Breaking changes in merge requests
breaking.subtitle: What a merge request on a spec does when it removes an operation, adds a required parameter or drops a response a client relies on. The changes are listed on its API changes tab either way.

off.label: Off
off.body: No readiness check and no gate. The diff is still shown.

warn.label: Warn
warn.body: The merge widget names the breaking changes; anyone who may merge still can.

block.label: Block
block.body: A merge is refused until a workspace admin acknowledges the breaking changes. A later push needs a new acknowledgement.

apiDiff.noChanges: No API changes. Every operation a client calls is unchanged.
apiDiff.noneShown: No changes of the selected severity.
apiDiff.affectedPages: Pages that may now be wrong

quality.scored: {scored} of {total} page scored | {scored} of {total} pages scored
quality.unscored: {n} not scored yet | {n} not scored yet

empty.title: No page has been scored yet

empty.run: Run the auditor from AI settings
empty.askAdmin: A workspace admin can run the auditor from AI settings.

history.title: Over time
history.hint: The average as it stood at the end of each audit day. Below {threshold}, the auditor reports a page.
history.summary: Score went from {from} on {start} to {to} on {end}
history.single: One audit so far, on {date}. The line starts with the second.

dimensions.title: Where the points go
dimensions.hint: The mean of each dimension over the pages where it could be measured.

clarity.label: Clarity
clarity.hint: Is it easy to follow — structure, sentences, defined terms.

completeness.label: Completeness
completeness.hint: Does it cover what a page like this needs, without gaps or placeholders.

links.label: Links
links.hint: Do its links to other pages resolve to a page that exists.

ownership.label: Ownership
ownership.hint: Does the page have an owner who answers for it.

duplication.label: Duplication
duplication.hint: Is it distinct from every other page, or does another say the same thing.

style.label: Style
style.hint: Does it follow the styleguide that applies to its project.

rules.title: Rules broken most
rules.hint: Styleguide rules the newest scores cite.
rules.none: No styleguide rule is broken on a scored page.

rail.stale: The page changed after this score; it is re-scored at the next audit.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: How people sign in, and what was done with elevated rights.
security.adminOnly: Only workspace admins can see the security settings.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.hint: Graph queries, access-control changes and bypasses, and sign-ins. Newest first.
audit.platformHint: Includes sign-ins and other events that belong to no workspace.

providers.title: Identity providers
providers.hint: Sign people in with your organization’s OpenID Connect, SAML 2.0 or, where enabled, LDAP directory. New providers start disabled.
providers.disabled: Single sign-on is not enabled on this instance. An operator turns it on with AUTH_SSO_ENABLED=true (and AUTH_MODE=api-key).
providers.formHint: Register the redirect URI shown after saving as an allowed redirect in the provider’s client.
providers.name: Button label
providers.secretStored: Stored — leave empty to keep it
providers.secretsNotWritable: Secrets cannot be stored: SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set on the server.
providers.allowedDomainsHint: Comma-separated. Accounts are linked or created only for verified addresses on these domains.
providers.jitHint: Otherwise only people who already have an account can sign in.
providers.showOnLogin: Show a button on the sign-in page
providers.platformWideToggle: Offer on every workspace’s sign-in page (platform-wide)
providers.testFailed: Could not read the discovery document: {error}
providers.removeBody: People who signed in with it are signed out, and their link to it is forgotten.
providers.formHintSaml: After saving, give the identity provider the SP metadata URL shown in the list, or its entity ID and ACS URL.
providers.idpCertHint: PEM, including the BEGIN CERTIFICATE line. During a key rollover, paste both certificates.
providers.attributeMapHint: Which assertion attributes hold the person’s details. Leave a field empty to try the usual names.
providers.groupsAttributeHint: Without a groups attribute, no groups are read and group mapping does not apply.
providers.allowIdpInitiated: Accept sign-ins started from the identity provider’s app portal
providers.allowIdpInitiatedHint: Each assertion is still accepted only once, and only while it is fresh.
providers.testOkSaml: Configuration is valid. IdP entity ID {issuer}
providers.formHintLdap: People sign in with their directory username and password. After saving, use Test to check that the service account can search the base DN.
providers.bindDnHint: The account that searches for people. Leave empty to search anonymously.
providers.userFilterHint: Write {placeholder} where the typed username goes. Leave empty to match uid, mail, sAMAccountName or userPrincipalName.
providers.attributeMapHintLdap: Which entry attributes hold the person’s details. Leave a field empty for mail, displayName (or cn) and memberOf.
providers.groupsAttributeHintLdap: Group mappings match the full group DN, for example cn=editors,ou=groups,dc=corp,dc=example.
providers.testOkLdap: Bound and searched the base DN at {issuer}

groupMapping.title: Group mapping
groupMapping.hint: Give people a workspace role from the groups your identity provider sends. The highest mapped role wins. Changes apply at each person’s next sign-in, and roles you set by hand on the Access page are never changed.
groupMapping.noProviders: Add an identity provider first — a mapping names the provider whose groups it reads.
groupMapping.operator: Also make them trusted operators (graph queries)
groupMapping.removeBody: Roles it granted stay until people sign in again.
groupMapping.empty: No groups mapped yet. Without a mapping, sign-ins get the provider’s role for new members, if it has one.
groupMapping.presetClaim: This provider has no groups claim set, so the preset’s default claim is read.

mode.additive: Additive: sign-in only ever raises a role. Nothing is taken away when a group disappears.
mode.authoritative: Authoritative: each sign-in sets the role exactly as the groups say, and removes the membership when no group maps.

groupMapping.disabled: Single sign-on and SCIM provisioning are both off on this instance. An operator turns them on with AUTH_SSO_ENABLED or AUTH_SCIM_ENABLED.
groupMapping.scimHint: A SCIM group's mapping applies at once to everyone in it. Provisioned people in no mapped group get the default role from the Provisioning tab.
groupMapping.removeBodyScim: Its members drop to the provisioning default role now.

domains.title: Domains
domains.hint: Prove that your organization owns an email domain, then require single sign-on for every address on it: password sign-in, signup and password reset stop working for those addresses.
domains.claimed: Claimed {domain}. Publish the DNS record to verify it.
domains.publish: Add this TXT record at your DNS provider, then press Verify. It is also checked every 15 minutes for a week.

verifyErrors.no-record: No TXT record found at {record} yet. DNS changes can take a while to appear.
verifyErrors.mismatch: A TXT record exists at {record}, but its value is not the one shown here.
verifyErrors.lookup-failed: DNS could not be reached just now. Try again in a minute.

domains.enforceTitle: Require single sign-on for every address on {domain}?
domains.enforceBody: Password sign-in stops working for them at once, except for break-glass addresses.
domains.enforcedOn: Single sign-on is now required on {domain}
domains.enforcedHint: People on this domain sign in only through single sign-on. Break-glass addresses set by the operator still work.
domains.notEnforcedHint: Verified, but passwords still work. Turn this on once people have signed in with SSO at least once.
domains.removeBody: Passwords work again for its addresses at once.

policy.title: Sign-in policy
policy.hint: Rules for reaching this workspace, checked on every request — the web app, API keys, MCP clients and live updates alike.
policy.ssoOff: Single sign-on is not enabled on this instance (AUTH_SSO_ENABLED), so the SSO settings below cannot apply. The session age limit still does.
policy.ssoEnforced: Require single sign-on for this workspace
policy.ssoEnforcedHint: Only sessions opened through {providers} reach this workspace. Everyone else is asked to sign in again through SSO.
policy.noProviders: Enable an identity provider for this workspace first.
policy.notApplied: Saved, but not applied: single sign-on is off on this instance.
policy.allowApiKeysHint: Keys keep working for scripts and MCP clients. Turn this off to accept only SSO sessions.
policy.allowPasswordForAdmins: Let platform admins use a password on enforced domains
policy.allowPasswordForAdminsHint: A way in for the people who fix SSO when it breaks. Platform admins can always reach the workspace; this decides whether they may sign in with a password.
policy.sessionMaxAgeHint: Sessions older than this must sign in again to reach this workspace. Sessions on this instance last {ttl} hours at most.
policy.sessionMaxAgeClamped: This is no shorter than the instance’s {ttl}-hour session lifetime, so it has no effect.
policy.breakGlass: Platform admins pass these rules, and every time they do it is recorded in the audit log. Addresses in AUTH_BREAK_GLASS_EMAILS can always use a password.
policy.enforceBody: Everyone signed in with a password is asked to sign in again through SSO.

lockout.password-session: You are signed in with a password, so this would lock you out. Sign in through the workspace’s identity provider first, then save.
lockout.foreign-provider: You signed in through a provider this workspace does not use, so this would lock you out.
lockout.api-key: You are using an API key, which this policy would block.
lockout.session-too-old: Your session is older than the limit you set, so this would sign you out of the workspace. Sign in again first.

scim.title: Provisioning (SCIM)
scim.hint: Let your identity provider create, update and deactivate this workspace's people over SCIM 2.0. Give it the base URL and a token. Deactivating someone in the IdP removes their membership and signs them out; roles you set by hand on the Access page stay.
scim.disabled: SCIM provisioning is off on this instance. An operator turns it on with AUTH_SCIM_ENABLED.
scim.defaultRoleHint: What a provisioned person gets when none of their groups is mapped on the Group mapping tab. Changing it re-applies to everyone provisioned.
scim.freshHint: Copy it into your identity provider now. It is not shown again: only a hash is stored.
scim.empty: No tokens yet. Create one per identity provider.
scim.revokeBody: The identity provider gets 401 from its next request.

releaseTags.title: Releases
releaseTags.subtitle: Name a point in time — a release, an audit — so the graph and search can show what the knowledge base said then.
releaseTags.name: Name
releaseTags.badName: Use letters, digits and . _ - / only, up to 64.
releaseTags.empty: Add one to read the graph and search as they stood at that point.
releaseTags.deleteBody: Only the name goes. What the knowledge base said at that point stays, and can still be read by date.

conflicts.title: Contradictions
conflicts.subtitle: Passages in two pages that say different things about the same thing. Found by the arbiter; decided by people.

toast.dismissed: Dismissed — it stays dismissed if found again

empty.hint: The arbiter agent compares passages across pages and lists the ones that disagree here. Run it, schedule it, or trigger it on every indexed page from its settings.

trafficHint.assisted: Read by the in-app assistant or a chat bot for a person
trafficHint.agent: Read through an API key, MCP or a background agent

analytics.viewsChartLabel: Views per day over {n} days, by who read: people, assistant, agents
analytics.notCollecting: No reads recorded yet in this workspace.

project.title: Reading
project.deadHint: Older than {n} days, unopened in the app and returned by no search in that time.
project.deadNotYet: Shows once reads have been counted for {n} days.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.subtitle: How the workspace is read and searched: by people, by the assistant for them, and by agents.
analytics.adminOnly: Usage analytics is for workspace admins: it shows what people searched for.
analytics.recordingOff: Recording is off for this workspace. The numbers below stop at the moment it was turned off.

views.label: Views
views.hint: Page opens in the range, from every channel the filter keeps

uniqueReaders.label: Readers
uniqueReaders.hint: Distinct readers. Browsers that send Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control count as views only

medianRead.label: Median read
medianRead.hint: Active reading time of a page opened in the app

searches.label: Searches
searches.hint: A reader repeating one query within 10 seconds counts once

zeroResult.label: Found nothing
zeroResult.hint: Share of searches that returned no results

clickThrough.label: Click-through
clickThrough.hint: Share of searches in the app that found something and were followed by opening a result

assistantQuestions.label: Assistant questions
assistantQuestions.hint: Questions people asked the in-app assistant

mcpCalls.label: MCP calls
mcpCalls.hint: Tool calls agents made over MCP

search.topHint: Click-through and the mean rank of the opened result count searches in the app only.
search.zeroResultHint: Queries that returned no results: pages that may be missing.
search.noClickHint: Searches in the app whose results nobody opened.

agents.keysHint: MCP calls, page reads and searches per key. Shown by name and prefix only.
agents.noKeys: No API key was used in this range.
agents.questionsChartLabel: Questions asked of the assistant per day over {n} days
agents.noQuestions: Nobody asked the assistant anything in this range.
agents.operationsHint: Every AI call in the workspace, by what it was for.

settings.title: Recording and retention
settings.intro: The deployment sets a ceiling: a workspace can turn recording off and keep rows for less time, never more.

recording.label: Record usage
recording.hint: Page views, searches and MCP calls. Off, nothing new is recorded; existing rows stay until retention removes them.

retention.label: Keep rows for
retention.hint: Older rows are deleted every hour. A search keeps its text for {text}, then only its hash.
retention.belowDead: Shorter than the {n}-day dead-page window: the unread and dead lists will never match a page.
retention.clamped: Longer than the deployment allows: {n} days will apply.

workItems.sendHint: Creates a ticket with a link back here, or attaches one that exists. Status then moves both ways.
workItems.noTrackers: No tracker connector here yet. An admin can connect Jira, GitHub or GitLab under Connectors.

settings.routesHint: A project's "Send to tracker" goes to this connector. Without a route, people pick a tracker each time and no rule creates tickets.
settings.mapHint: How this tracker's statuses read as ours. Leave a field empty to keep the default shown in it.
settings.outbound: When it changes here, move the ticket to
settings.inboundDefaults: Defaults: {list}. Tracker statuses are matched without regard to case.
settings.peopleHint: Tracker accounts seen here, and who each one is in this workspace. Used to say who closed a ticket, and to let a mapped editor's close clear a page's flag. Nobody is assigned anything.

workItems.everyTracker: This already has a ticket on every tracker connected here.

rules.title: Handoff to trackers
rules.intro: Hand these off to a tracker without anyone pressing Send to tracker. A ticket goes to the project's tracker route, so a project without one gets none. Each object gets one ticket, once.

issues.label: Reported issues
issues.hint: High: a report of wrong content, or one reported by three or more people. Medium also includes stale and missing reports, and any reported twice.

conflicts.label: Knowledge conflicts
conflicts.hint: Every open conflict between two sources.

verification.label: Flagged pages
verification.hint: A page marked outdated, or also one with a check requested.

rules.ceiling: This deployment creates at most {n} ticket per sweep (every ~15 s), across all workspaces. A large backlog is handed off over a few minutes. | This deployment creates at most {n} tickets per sweep (every ~15 s), across all workspaces. A large backlog is handed off over a few minutes.
rules.stopped: This deployment has handoff rules switched off (WORK_ITEM_AUTOCREATE_MAX_PER_TICK=0 or WORK_ITEM_SYNC_ENABLED=false). Saved rules apply once they are back on.

imageViewer.title: Image preview
imageViewer.hint: Click the image to see it at full size, drag to move around it, and use the arrow keys to go to the next or previous image.

diagramViewer.title: Diagram preview
diagramViewer.hint: Click the diagram to see it at its own size, drag to move around it, use + and − or Ctrl and the wheel to zoom, 0 to fit, and the arrow keys to go to the next or previous diagram.

pwa.offlineDescription: Pages already open stay readable. Anything that needs the server will fail until the connection returns.
